purpose: Eltrombopag is used to raise your platelet count when it is dangerously low. It is used for conditions like chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), aplastic anemia, and low platelets caused by hepatitis C treatment. Having more platelets helps your blood clot properly and reduces your risk of serious bleeding.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a hormone called thrombopoietin that tells your bone marrow to produce platelets. Eltrombopag works like that hormone by attaching to the same receptor in your bone marrow and signaling it to make more platelets. Think of it as sending a 'make more platelets' message directly to your bone marrow.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, diarrhea, muscle or joint aches, upper respiratory infections, cough, fatigue, and changes in liver blood test results. Some people also notice changes in hair or skin color.
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver problems, so your doctor will monitor your liver with regular blood tests. It can also increase the risk of blood clots forming in your veins or arteries, which can be dangerous. It may rarely cause cataracts (clouding of the eye lens), so eye check-ups are recommended. Taking it with dairy products, antacids, or calcium-rich foods can reduce how well it is absorbed — always take it on an empty stomach and away from these foods. Do not take more than prescribed, as too many platelets can also be harmful.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 50 mg taken by mouth once daily on an empty stomach. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your platelet count — doses can range from 25 mg to 75 mg per day. For some patients of East Asian descent, the starting dose may be lower (25 mg). Always take it at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after eating dairy, antacids, or vitamins/minerals containing calcium, iron, aluminum, or magnesium.
